text:
emily: Deploybot just flagged the canary for service-connector:2025.06.10-canary during the change window.
deploybot: [automated] Canary blocked: SBOM policy violation (license) and vuln-scan: image redwood/service-connector:2025.06.10-canary
deploybot: License issue: detected package 'old-logger' v1.0.0 with GPL-2.0-only in runtime layer (policy LCN-2).
deploybot: Vulnerability: CVE-2025-9999 - old-logger v1.0.0 - CVSS 7.8 - usage: logging formatter (runtime).
marco: hmm license + vuln in runtime package. Is old-logger coming from our base-image or app layer?
priya: quick SBOM snippet from registry: ```{"packages":[{"name":"old-logger","version":"1.0.0","layer":"app","license":"GPL-2.0-only"}]}```
emily: license alone would block for enterprise customers. We also have an EU change freeze in 45m.
release-manager: Legal will want to block if GPL in runtime for this service. @legal?
legal: GPL-2.0-only in runtime is a hard no for redistributable artifacts. We need a mitigation plan: replace or remove the package before global rollout. Regional carve-out could be considered if we document risk and restrict to internal-only test fleets.
priya: mitigation options: 1) vendorize logger (remove license) 2) swap to mit-licensed logger (requires minor code change) 3) rollback to previous stable tag 2025.05.20-stable
oncall-sre: operational impact: rollback ~8m, vendorize ~40-60m dev + CI + scan.
marco: can we do a partial promote? keep us-east canary, block EU/APAC?
deploybot: regional promote supported. Command: `/deploy promote --env=us-east --service=service-connector --tag=2025.06.10-canary`
emily: I don't love divergent fleets but it's reasonable for risk containment. Any objections?
legal: regional carve-out okay for canaries only, not customers. Must not be visible to enterprise tenants.
priya: swapping to mit-logger is a 15-line change. I'll open a PR now (hotfix/logger-mit).
marco: alternative quick path: pin to previous image without old-logger. Tag: `2025.05.20-stable`. That's fastest.
emily: prefer minimal customer impact. Marco, please execute a regional rollback for EU and APAC and keep US canary running.
marco: on it. `/deploy rollback --env=eu --service=service-connector --to-tag=2025.05.20-stable`
deploybot: [automated] Rollback initiated for EU.
deploybot: Rollback: shards 1-4 complete.
deploybot: EU rollback complete. service-connector at 2025.05.20-stable.
emily: APAC next when EU confirmed.
marco: rolling APAC now.
deploybot: APAC rollback complete.
priya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/pr/3421 hotfix/logger-mit - building. CI: `BUILD OK`
sbom-bot: SBOM generation and signing pending for new image build.
priya: attaching cosign in CI step now.
marco: security note: policy SBN-5 requires signed SBOM + license check green before any global promote.
release-manager: release notes: do not mention specifics. Use neutral language: "postponed global canary rollout due to internal security checks; targeted rollback in some regions". Legal confirm?
legal: approved neutral wording. No mention of GPL or CVE in customer-facing notes.
oncall-sre: monitoring: set alert to watch for telemetry divergence due to regional differences.
emily: timeline: if PR builds + SBOM signed + scans clear within 90m, we can attempt global re-promote in next change window. Otherwise schedule for next available window.
marco: created incident doc: INCIDENT-2025-0610-4 - License/vuln block during canary - assigned to release and security.
priya: build passed, SBOM generated and cosign attached. vuln-scan: in progress.
sbom-bot: SBOM policy check: PASS (license OK), vuln-scan: PASS
deploybot: Artifact signed and verified. Ready for promote.
emily: thanks. We'll wait for release-manager to greenlight global promote.
release-manager: greenlight for global promote given SBOM signed + scans pass. Proceed with promote in 5m.
deploybot: Promoting global canary: `/deploy promote --env=global --service=service-connector --tag=2025.06.10-canary`
deploybot: Global promote started. Progress 2/10 regions.
deploybot: Global promote complete. All regions on 2025.06.10-canary.
emily: closing thread. Follow-up: postmortem required documenting how a GPL dependency landed in runtime SBOM. Assign to priya + supply-chain team.
 (end)
